definition: The three projections at the heart of attention.
details: The three projections at the heart of attention. Each token emits a query ("what am I looking for"), a key ("what do I contain"), and a value ("what do I contribute"). Attention scores are query-key similarities; the output is a score-weighted sum of values.

explainer.lead: Query, key and value are the three projections at the heart of attention. They matter because attention scores and outputs are computed entirely from them.

tiers.eli5: Each word asks a question (query), says what it knows (key), and offers what it can share (value); attention matches questions to knowledge and collects the matching offers.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build attention by projecting each token into a query, a key and a value. A pitfall is misreading the roles: scores come from query-key similarity, not from values.
tiers.paperLevel: Attention scores are query-key similarities; the output is a score-weighted sum of values. Each token emits a query ('what am I looking for'), a key ('what do I contain') and a value ('what do I contribute').

explainer.example: For one token, its query is compared with every token's key to get scores, and those scores weight the sum of all values to produce the output.
